```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 1440
library(shiny)

## ------------------------------------------------------------------- model
## One covariate x, four tanh hidden units, log link, Poisson counts:
##   a_j = w_j1 x + w_j0,  h_j = tanh(a_j),  eta = v_0 + sum_j v_j h_j,
##   lambda = exp(eta).
## theta = (w11..wJ1,  w10..wJ0,  v1..vJ,  v0)
J <- 4
NP <- 3 * J + 1                                  # number of weights
NAMES <- c(paste0("w", 1:J, "1"), paste0("w", 1:J, "0"), paste0("v", 1:J), "v0")
BIASIDX <- c(J + 1:J, NP)                        # the intercepts w_j0 and v_0
## two bumps in the mean: units 1, 2 switch on and off over (-2.2, -0.8),
## units 3, 4 over (0.8, 2.2), so lambda(x) has two modes
TRUE_THETA <- c(2.5, 2.5, 2.5, 2.5,   5.5, 2, -2, -5.5,   1.2, -1.2, 1.0, -1.0,   -0.5)

fwd <- function(th, x) {
  H <- tanh(outer(x, th[1:J]) + rep(th[J + 1:J], each = length(x)))
  list(H = H, eta = as.vector(th[3 * J + 1] + H %*% th[2 * J + 1:J]))
}
lambda_fun <- function(th, x) exp(fwd(th, x)$eta)

## the scaled units v_j h_j(x), one column per hidden unit
unit_terms <- function(th, x) sweep(fwd(th, x)$H, 2, th[2 * J + 1:J], "*")

## average Poisson negative log-likelihood (the log y! term dropped)
nll <- function(th, x, y) {
  e <- fwd(th, x)$eta
  v <- mean(exp(e) - y * e)
  if (is.finite(v)) v else Inf
}

## its gradient by backpropagation:  delta_eta -> delta_a -> weights
nll_grad <- function(th, x, y) {
  E <- fwd(th, x)
  d_eta <- exp(E$eta) - y                                   # n
  d_a   <- (1 - E$H^2) * outer(d_eta, th[2 * J + 1:J])      # n x J
  c(colSums(d_a * x),                                       # w_j1
    colSums(d_a),                                           # w_j0
    as.vector(crossprod(E$H, d_eta)),                       # v_j
    sum(d_eta)) / length(x)                                 # v_0
}

make_data <- function(n, seed) {
  set.seed(100 + seed)
  x <- runif(n, -3, 3)
  y <- rpois(n, lambda_fun(TRUE_THETA, x))
  ## a fixed vertical offset, drawn once with the data, so the points stay put
  list(x = x, y = y, yj = y + runif(n, -0.12, 0.12))
}

rand_start <- function(seed) {
  set.seed(2000 + seed)
  c(rnorm(3 * J, 0, 1), 0)
}

## ------------------------------------------------------- Wolfe line search
line_search <- function(f, g, x, d, a0 = 1, c1 = 1e-4, c2 = 0.9) {
  f0 <- f(x); gd0 <- sum(g(x) * d)
  if (!is.finite(gd0) || gd0 >= 0) return(list(alpha = 0, ok = FALSE))
  lo <- 0; hi <- Inf; a <- a0
  for (it in 1:60) {
    fa <- f(x + a * d)
    if (!is.finite(fa) || fa > f0 + c1 * a * gd0) {
      hi <- a; a <- 0.5 * (lo + hi)
    } else {
      if (sum(g(x + a * d) * d) < c2 * gd0) {
        lo <- a
        a <- if (is.finite(hi)) 0.5 * (lo + hi) else min(2 * a, 1e4)
      } else {
        return(list(alpha = a, ok = TRUE))
      }
    }
    if (a < 1e-14) return(list(alpha = 0, ok = FALSE))
  }
  list(alpha = a, ok = (a > 0))
}

## ------------------------------------------------------------- algorithms
## the methods that step through mini-batches: one iteration is one epoch
MINIBATCH <- c("sgdls", "mom", "adam")
## Row k of P, G, F is the state after k - 1 steps; A[k] is the step length
## that led to it.
run_alg <- function(alg, th0, x, y, maxit, lr = 0.1, mom = 0.9, m = 20,
                    tol = 1e-6, patience = Inf, rtol = 1e-5) {
  p <- length(th0)
  f <- function(th) nll(th, x, y)
  g <- function(th) nll_grad(th, x, y)
  P <- G <- matrix(NA_real_, maxit + 1, p)
  Fv <- AL <- rep(NA_real_, maxit + 1)
  th <- th0; B <- diag(p)
  g_prev <- d_prev <- s_prev <- NULL
  n <- 0; note <- "maximum number of iterations reached"
  best_f <- Inf; best_k <- 1                  # the best loss so far, and when it was reached
  ## state for the fixed-rate rules
  n_obs <- length(x); m <- max(1, min(m, n_obs))
  capped <- FALSE
  if (alg %in% MINIBATCH) {                  # keep the number of mini-batch steps in check
    cap <- max(1, floor(100000 / ceiling(n_obs / m)))
    if (maxit > cap) { maxit <- cap; capped <- TRUE }
  }
  vel <- m1 <- m2 <- numeric(p)              # momentum velocity; Adam moments
  tt <- 0                                    # mini-batch updates so far (Adam)
  if (alg %in% MINIBATCH) set.seed(11)

  for (k in 1:(maxit + 1)) {
    gk <- g(th); fk <- f(th)
    P[k, ] <- th; G[k, ] <- gk; Fv[k] <- fk; n <- k
    if (!is.finite(fk) || !all(is.finite(gk))) { note <- "diverged"; break }
    if (tol > 0 && sqrt(sum(gk^2)) < tol) {
      note <- paste0("converged: gradient norm < ", format(tol)); break
    }
    ## no stopping rule can be exact for a noisy method, so every method also stops when the
    ## full-data loss has not improved by a fraction rtol for `patience` iterations
    if (k == 1 || fk < best_f - rtol * abs(best_f)) { best_f <- fk; best_k <- k }
    if (k - best_k >= patience) {
      note <- paste0("stopped: the loss has not improved by ", 100 * rtol, "% in ",
                     patience, " iterations"); break
    }
    if (k > maxit) break

    if (alg == "gdfix") {                    # full-batch gradient, fixed learning rate
      AL[k + 1] <- lr
      th <- th - lr * gk
      next
    }

    if (alg %in% MINIBATCH) {                # one iteration is one epoch: a shuffled pass
      perm <- sample.int(n_obs)              # of mini-batch steps over all the data, so
      al <- numeric(0)                       # it costs about one full-batch gradient
      for (s0 in seq(1, n_obs, by = m)) {
        idx <- perm[s0:min(s0 + m - 1, n_obs)]
        xb <- x[idx]; yb <- y[idx]
        gb <- nll_grad(th, xb, yb)               # the gradient of mini-batch B_k
        if (alg == "sgdls") {                # backtracking line search on the batch loss
          fb <- nll(th, xb, yb); a <- lr; gg <- sum(gb^2)
          for (j in 1:30) {
            fa <- nll(th - a * gb, xb, yb)
            if (is.finite(fa) && fa <= fb - 1e-4 * a * gg) break
            a <- a / 2
          }
          al <- c(al, a)
          th <- th - a * gb
        } else if (alg == "mom") {           # heavy ball on the batch gradient
          vel <- mom * vel - lr * gb
          th <- th + vel
        } else {                             # Adam on the batch gradient
          tt <- tt + 1
          m1 <- 0.9 * m1 + 0.1 * gb
          m2 <- 0.999 * m2 + 0.001 * gb^2
          th <- th - lr * (m1 / (1 - 0.9^tt)) / (sqrt(m2 / (1 - 0.999^tt)) + 1e-8)
        }
      }
      AL[k + 1] <- if (alg == "sgdls") mean(al) else lr
      next
    }

    if (alg == "gd") {
      d <- -gk
    } else if (alg == "cg") {
      if (is.null(d_prev)) {
        d <- -gk
      } else {
        yk <- gk - g_prev
        beta <- max(0, sum(gk * yk) / max(sum(g_prev^2), 1e-300))   # PR+
        d <- -gk + beta * d_prev
      }
      if (sum(gk * d) > -1e-12) d <- -gk                           # restart
    } else {                                                       # BFGS
      if (!is.null(s_prev)) {
        yk <- gk - g_prev; sy <- sum(s_prev * yk)
        if (sy > 1e-10) {
          if (k == 2) B <- (sy / sum(yk^2)) * diag(p)    # scale the first B
          rho <- 1 / sy
          V <- diag(p) - rho * outer(s_prev, yk)
          B <- V %*% B %*% t(V) + rho * outer(s_prev, s_prev)
        }
      }
      d <- -as.vector(B %*% gk)
      if (sum(gk * d) > -1e-12) { B <- diag(p); d <- -gk }
    }

    a0 <- if (alg == "bfgs" && k > 1) 1 else min(1, 1 / sqrt(sum(d^2)))
    ls <- line_search(f, g, th, d, a0)
    if (!ls$ok && alg != "gd") {             # restart from steepest descent before giving up
      d <- -gk; B <- diag(p); d_prev <- s_prev <- g_prev <- NULL
      ls <- line_search(f, g, th, d, min(1, 1 / sqrt(sum(d^2))))
    }
    if (!ls$ok) { note <- "line search failed"; break }
    AL[k + 1] <- ls$alpha
    s_prev <- ls$alpha * d; g_prev <- gk; d_prev <- d
    th <- th + s_prev
  }
  if (capped && grepl("^maximum", note))
    note <- paste0("stopped after ", maxit, " epochs (100000 mini-batch steps)")
  i <- seq_len(n)
  list(P = P[i, , drop = FALSE], G = G[i, , drop = FALSE], F = Fv[i],
       A = AL[i], n = n, note = note)
}

ALGS <- c("Gradient descent, fixed learning rate"     = "gdfix",
          "Gradient descent + line search"            = "gd",
          "Conjugate gradient (Polak-Ribiere+)"       = "cg",
          "BFGS (quasi-Newton)"                       = "bfgs",
          "SGD + line search (on each mini-batch)"    = "sgdls",
          "SGD + momentum"                            = "mom",
          "SGD + Adam"                                = "adam")

alg_name <- function(a) if (a == "none") "none" else names(ALGS)[ALGS == a]

## --------------------------------------------------------- network layout
## Weights sit on the edges; each intercept is a node of its own, a box with
## the value and its arrows, hung on the neuron it shifts.
NX <- c(0.07, 0.50)                                 # (x, y) of the input node
YH <- seq(0.88, 0.12, length.out = J); XH <- 0.60   # hidden nodes
NO <- c(1.13, 0.50)                                 # output node
at <- function(p, q, f) p + f * (q - p)             # a point along an edge
## hidden intercepts hang above the upper half of the hidden nodes and below the rest
YB <- YH + rep(c(0.14, -0.14), each = J / 2)
BIAS <- c(rep(0.56, J), 1.00)                       # x of the intercept boxes
BIASY <- c(YB, 0.17)                                # y of the intercept boxes
## where each weight's value and arrows sit
ADJ <- local({
  hj <- lapply(1:J, function(j) c(XH, YH[j]))
  pos <- c(lapply(1:J, function(j) at(NX, hj[[j]], 0.50)),    # w_j1: x -> h_j
           lapply(1:J, function(j) c(BIAS[j], BIASY[j])),     # w_j0: box on h_j
           lapply(1:J, function(j) at(hj[[j]], NO, 0.50)),    # v_j: h_j -> out
           list(c(BIAS[J + 1], BIASY[J + 1])))                # v_0: box on output
  data.frame(idx = 1:NP, sym = NAMES,
             x = sapply(pos, `[`, 1), y = sapply(pos, `[`, 2),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
})
## the arrows beside each value (also the click targets): up / down beside an
## edge weight, left / right beside an intercept box
AX <- 0.104                                  # arrow offset from the value
isb <- ADJ$idx %in% BIASIDX
ARROWS <- rbind(
  data.frame(idx = ADJ$idx, dir = +1, horiz = isb,
             ax = ifelse(isb, ADJ$x + AX, ADJ$x + AX),
             ay = ifelse(isb, ADJ$y, ADJ$y + 0.028)),
  data.frame(idx = ADJ$idx, dir = -1, horiz = isb,
             ax = ifelse(isb, ADJ$x - AX, ADJ$x + AX),
             ay = ifelse(isb, ADJ$y, ADJ$y - 0.028)))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------- colours
## Diverging ramp: blue = negative, red = positive, depth by magnitude.
DIV <- colorRampPalette(c("#08306B", "#2171B5", "#6BAED6", "#DEEBF7",
                          "#F7F7F7",
                          "#FEE0D2", "#FC9272", "#CB181D", "#67000D"))(201)

## compander: maps v in [-vmax, vmax] to [-1, 1], boosting small values
tone <- function(v, vmax, k) {
  u <- pmax(-1, pmin(1, v / vmax))
  sign(u) * log1p(k * abs(u)) / log1p(k)
}
hcol <- function(v, vmax, k) DIV[round((tone(v, vmax, k) + 1) * 100) + 1]

draw_net <- function(v, vmax, k, main, arrows = TRUE, digits = 2) {
  col <- hcol(v, vmax, k); lw <- 0.8 + 6 * abs(tone(v, vmax, k))
  plot.new(); plot.window(c(0, 1.2), c(-0.25, 1.08))
  title(main = main, cex.main = 1.05)
  H <- cbind(XH, YH)
  ## edges, each carrying one weight: x -> h_j (w_j1), h_j -> output (v_j)
  for (j in 1:J) {
    segments(NX[1], NX[2], H[j, 1], H[j, 2], col = col[j],     lwd = lw[j],     lend = 1)
    segments(H[j, 1], H[j, 2], NO[1], NO[2], col = col[2 * J + j], lwd = lw[2 * J + j], lend = 1)
  }
  ## intercept nodes: a thin arrow from each box to the neuron it shifts
  tgt <- rbind(H, NO)
  for (i in seq_along(BIASIDX)) {
    b <- ADJ[BIASIDX[i], ]
    dy <- sign(tgt[i, 2] - b$y)
    if (i == J + 1) arrows(b$x, b$y + 0.03, NO[1] - 0.03, NO[2] - 0.03, length = 0.08,
                       col = "grey45", lwd = 1.4)
    else arrows(b$x, b$y + dy * 0.035, tgt[i, 1], tgt[i, 2] - dy * 0.035,
                length = 0.08, col = "grey45", lwd = 1.4)
  }
  ## nodes
  points(rbind(NX, H, NO), pch = 21, cex = 3.2, bg = "white", lwd = 1.6)
  text(NX[1], NX[2], "x", font = 2)
  text(H[, 1], H[, 2], paste0("h", 1:J), cex = 0.8)
  text(NO[1], NO[2], expression(lambda), cex = 1.1)
  ## values: an intercept is a box coloured by its value; an edge weight is
  ## plain text on a white patch so the edge does not strike through it
  for (i in 1:NP) {
    b <- ADJ[i, ]; isb <- i %in% BIASIDX
    if (isb) rect(b$x - 0.075, b$y - 0.036, b$x + 0.075, b$y + 0.036,
                  col = col[i], border = "grey35")
    else rect(b$x - 0.072, b$y - 0.028, b$x + 0.072, b$y + 0.028,
              col = adjustcolor("white", 0.8), border = NA)
    dark <- abs(tone(v[i], vmax, k)) > 0.62
    text(b$x, b$y, sprintf(paste0("%s=%.", digits, "f"), b$sym, v[i]),
         cex = 0.85, font = if (isb) 1 else 2,
         col = if (isb) { if (dark) "white" else "black" }
               else if (dark) col[i] else "grey20")
  }
  if (arrows) for (r in seq_len(nrow(ARROWS))) {
    a <- ARROWS[r, ]
    if (a$horiz)                                   # left / right: -, +
      polygon(a$ax + a$dir * c(-0.013, -0.013, 0.015),
              a$ay + c(-0.033, 0.033, 0), col = "grey30", border = NA)
    else                                           # down / up: -, +
      polygon(a$ax + c(-0.026, 0.026, 0), a$ay + a$dir * c(-0.016, -0.016, 0.02),
              col = "grey30", border = NA)
  }
  ## signed colour bar
  xs <- seq(0.12, 1.08, length.out = 201)
  rect(xs, -0.24, xs + diff(xs)[1], -0.19, col = DIV, border = NA)
  lab <- formatC(vmax, format = "g", digits = 2)
  text(c(0.12, 0.60, 1.08), -0.16, c(paste0("-", lab), "0", paste0("+", lab)),
       cex = 0.72)
}

## --------------------------------------------------------------------- UI
## an icon-only playback button; the title shows as a tooltip
ctrl_btn <- function(id, icon_name, title, class = "btn-default")
  actionButton(id, NULL, icon = icon(icon_name), title = title, class = class,
               style = "flex: 1; padding: 6px 0;")

row_label <- function(txt)
  column(1, div(style = "padding-top: 28px;", tags$b(txt)))

## learning rates on a roughly logarithmic grid (rates need to range over orders of magnitude)
LRGRID <- c(1e-5, 3e-5, 1e-4, 3e-4, 1e-3, 3e-3, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1)
LRCHOICES <- setNames(as.character(LRGRID), format(LRGRID, scientific = FALSE, drop0trailing = TRUE))

## one optimizer: its menu, then the parameters that belong to the chosen method
opt_row <- function(s, selected, col, none = FALSE) {
  a <- paste0("input.alg", s)
  has_lr <- paste0("['gdfix', 'sgdls', 'mom', 'adam'].indexOf(", a, ") >= 0")
  has_b  <- paste0("['sgdls', 'mom', 'adam'].indexOf(", a, ") >= 0")
  fluidRow(
    column(1, div(style = paste0("padding-top: 28px; font-size: 20px; color: ", col, ";"),
                  tags$b(s))),
    column(3, selectInput(paste0("alg", s), "Optimizer",
                          choices = if (none) c("None" = "none", ALGS) else ALGS,
                          selected = selected, width = "100%")),
    column(8,
      conditionalPanel(has_lr,
        div(class = "steprule",
          div(selectInput(paste0("lr", s), "Learning rate (first step if line search)",
                          choices = LRCHOICES, selected = "0.3", width = "100%")),
          conditionalPanel(paste0(a, " == 'mom'"),
            div(sliderInput(paste0("mom", s), "Momentum", min = 0, max = 0.99,
                            value = 0.9, step = 0.01, width = "100%"))),
          conditionalPanel(has_b,
            div(selectInput(paste0("batch", s), "Mini-batch size",
                            choices = c("5" = 5, "10" = 10, "20" = 20, "50" = 50,
                                        "100" = 100, "all n (full batch)" = 1e6),
                            selected = 20, width = "100%"))))),
      conditionalPanel(paste0(has_lr, " == false && ", a, " != 'none'"),
        div(style = "padding-top: 28px;",
            helpText("The step length comes from a Wolfe line search."))))
  )
}

ui <- fluidPage(
  ## the iteration slider is the only state: the browser moves it (play timer, buttons,
  ## dragging), and the server just reads input$kshow
  tags$head(tags$script(HTML("
    var ktimer = null, kdrag = false, kself = false, kuser = 0;
    function kcur() { return parseInt($('#kshow').val()); }
    function kslider() { return $('#kshow').data('ionRangeSlider'); }
    function kset(v) {
      var s = kslider(); if (!s) return;
      kself = true;
      s.update({from: Math.max(s.options.min, Math.min(s.options.max, v))});
      $('#kshow').trigger('change'); kself = false; }
    function kplay(on) {
      if (ktimer) { clearInterval(ktimer); ktimer = null; }
      $('#play i').removeClass('fa-play fa-pause').addClass(on ? 'fa-pause' : 'fa-play');
      if (!on) return;
      var s = kslider(); if (s && kcur() >= s.options.max) kset(0);
      ktimer = setInterval(function() {
        if (kdrag || Date.now() - kuser < 600) return;   // the user is on the slider
        var s = kslider();
        if (kcur() >= s.options.max) kplay(false); else kset(kcur() + 1);
      }, 300); }
    ['mousedown', 'touchstart', 'pointerdown'].forEach(function(ev) {
      document.addEventListener(ev, function(e) {
        if ($(e.target).closest('.shiny-input-container').find('#kshow').length) {
          kdrag = true; kuser = Date.now(); } }, true); });
    ['mouseup', 'touchend', 'pointerup'].forEach(function(ev) {
      document.addEventListener(ev, function() { kdrag = false; kuser = Date.now(); }, true); });
    $(document).on('change', '#kshow', function() { if (!kself) kuser = Date.now(); });
    $(document).on('click', '#play', function() { kplay(!ktimer); });
    $(document).on('click', '#step',  function() { kplay(false); kset(kcur() + 1); });
    $(document).on('click', '#back',  function() { kplay(false); kset(kcur() - 1); });
    $(document).on('click', '#first', function() { kplay(false); kset(0); });
    $(document).on('click', '#toend', function() { kplay(false); kset(kslider().options.max); });
    Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('krun', function(m) {
      kplay(false);
      var s = kslider(); if (s) { s.update({max: m.max, from: 0}); $('#kshow').trigger('change'); }
      if (m.play) kplay(true); });
  "))),
  ## small text for the row of weight buttons
  tags$head(tags$style(HTML("
    .wbar .btn { font-size: 12px; padding: 3px 10px; }
    .wbar label { font-size: 12px; margin-bottom: 1px; }
    .wbar .form-group { margin-bottom: 0; }
    .wbar .selectize-input, .wbar select { font-size: 12px; min-height: 26px;
                                           padding: 3px 8px; }
    .steprule { display: flex; gap: 14px; }
    .steprule > div { flex: 1; min-width: 0; }"))),
  ## ---- control panel, at the top -------------------------------------------
  wellPanel(
    ## the data
    fluidRow(
      row_label("Setup"),
      column(2, sliderInput("n", "Sample size n", min = 50, max = 2000,
                            value = 150, step = 50, width = "100%")),
      column(2, selectInput("xscale", "Scale of x", choices = c("0.1" = 0.1, "1" = 1, "10" = 10, "100" = 100),
                            selected = 1, width = "100%")),
      column(2, div(style = "padding-top: 25px;",
                    actionButton("newdata", "Regenerate data",
                                 class = "btn-warning", style = "width:100%;")))
    ),
    hr(style = "margin: 4px 0 8px;"),
    ## two optimizers, each with its own settings: A (green) and B (blue)
    opt_row("A", "adam", "#2E8B57"),
    opt_row("B", "gd", "#1F5FBF", none = TRUE),
    hr(style = "margin: 4px 0 8px;"),
    ## how long to run them, the colour scale, the play buttons, the iteration shown
    fluidRow(
      row_label("Run"),
      column(1, selectInput("maxit", "Max iterations",
                            choices = c(10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000),
                            selected = 100, width = "100%")),
      column(1, selectInput("ctr", "Contrast",
                            choices = c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32), selected = 8,
                            width = "100%")),
      column(1, selectInput("gtol", "Stop: ||g|| <",
                            choices = c("0.1" = 0.1, "0.01" = 0.01, "1e-3" = 0.001,
                                        "1e-4" = 1e-4, "1e-6" = 1e-6, "1e-8" = 1e-8,
                                        "never" = 0),
                            selected = 1e-6, width = "100%")),
      column(1, selectInput("stall", "Stop if flat for",
                            choices = c("never" = Inf, "100 its" = 100, "50 its" = 50, "20 its" = 20),
                            selected = Inf, width = "100%")),
      column(3, div(style = "display: flex; gap: 4px; padding-top: 22px;",
                    ctrl_btn("first", "backward-fast", "Back to the start"),
                    ctrl_btn("back",  "backward-step", "One iteration back"),
                    ctrl_btn("play",  "play",          "Play / pause",
                             class = "btn-primary"),
                    ctrl_btn("step",  "forward-step",  "One iteration forward"),
                    ctrl_btn("toend", "forward-fast",  "To the end")),
             checkboxInput("autoplay", "Autoplay on change", FALSE)),
      column(3, sliderInput("kshow", "Iteration shown", min = 0, max = 100,
                            value = 0, step = 1, width = "100%"))
    )
  ),  fluidRow(
    ## ---- left: the network of values above the network of gradients -----
    column(6,
      div(class = "wbar",
          style = "display: flex; gap: 6px; align-items: flex-end; margin-bottom: 4px;",
          actionButton("settrue", "True Value", class = "btn-success"),
          actionButton("newstart", "Random"),
          actionButton("setzero", "Zero"),
          div(style = "width: 110px; margin-left: 6px;",
              selectInput("astep", "Adjust Size",
                          choices = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1),
                          selected = 0.25, width = "100%")),
          div(style = "width: 90px; margin-left: 6px;",
              selectInput("netsel", "Network of", choices = c("A", "B"), width = "100%"))),
      plotOutput("netv", height = "420px", click = "netv_click"),
      plotOutput("netg", height = "420px"),
      helpText("Click the up / down arrows beside a weight to change the ",
               "starting value (this restarts the run). The true values are ",
               "those that generated the data.")),
    ## ---- right: the fitted mean, and how the optimizer is doing -----------
    column(6,
      checkboxInput("showparts", "Show the units on the log scale", TRUE),
      plotOutput("fit", height = "380px"),
      conditionalPanel("input.showparts", plotOutput("eta", height = "250px")),
      plotOutput("conv", height = "230px"),
      radioButtons("lscale", NULL, inline = TRUE,
                   choices = c("log10 loss" = "log", "log10 (loss - smallest reached)" = "exc",
                               "loss" = "lin")),
      htmlOutput("info"))
  )
)

## ----------------------------------------------------------------- server
server <- function(input, output, session) {

  dseed <- reactiveVal(1); rseed <- reactiveVal(1)
  theta0 <- reactiveVal(rand_start(1))        # the starting weights

  observeEvent(input$newdata, dseed(dseed() + 1))
  ## a sensible starting learning rate for each fixed-rate method
  ## a sensible learning rate for the method and the scale of x: the curvature in a slope
  ## weight grows like s^2, and Adam's step is measured in the weight, which shrinks like 1 / s
  for (s in c("A", "B")) local({
    s <- s
    observeEvent(list(input[[paste0("alg", s)]], input$xscale), {
      a <- input[[paste0("alg", s)]]
      base <- c(gdfix = 0.1, sgdls = 0.1, mom = 0.03, adam = 0.1)[a]
      if (!is.null(a) && !is.na(base)) {
        v <- unname(base) / xsc()^(if (a == "adam") 1 else 2)
        r <- LRGRID[which.min(abs(log(LRGRID) - log(v)))]
        updateSelectInput(session, paste0("lr", s), selected = as.character(r))
      }
    })
  })
  observeEvent(input$setzero, theta0(rep(0, NP)))
  observeEvent(input$newstart, {
    rseed(rseed() + 1)
    th <- rand_start(rseed()); th[1:J] <- th[1:J] / xsc()   # random weights for x / s
    theta0(th)
  })
  ## an arrow click moves the nearest arrow's weight by one step
  observeEvent(input$netv_click, {
    cl <- input$netv_click
    d <- ((cl$x - ARROWS$ax) / 0.05)^2 + ((cl$y - ARROWS$ay) / 0.04)^2
    i <- which.min(d)
    if (d[i] < 2) {
      th <- theta0()
      th[ARROWS$idx[i]] <- th[ARROWS$idx[i]] + ARROWS$dir[i] * as.numeric(input$astep)
      theta0(th)
    }
  })

  ## the predictor on a different scale: x -> s x, with the slope weights of the generating
  ## network divided by s, so the true curve is the same function of x / s
  xsc <- reactive(if (is.null(input$xscale)) 1 else as.numeric(input$xscale))
  TT <- reactive({ th <- TRUE_THETA; th[1:J] <- th[1:J] / xsc(); th })
  observeEvent(input$settrue, theta0(TT()))
  ## a new scale of x keeps the starting curve: the slope weights change with it
  xprev <- reactiveVal(1)
  observeEvent(input$xscale, {
    th <- theta0(); th[1:J] <- th[1:J] * xprev() / xsc(); xprev(xsc()); theta0(th)
  }, ignoreInit = TRUE)
  DAT <- reactive({
    D <- make_data(input$n, dseed())
    D$x <- D$x * xsc()
    D
  })
  ## one run for each optimizer, from the same start on the same data
  mkrun <- function(s) reactive({
    D <- DAT(); a <- input[[paste0("alg", s)]]
    if (is.null(a) || a == "none") return(NULL)
    fixed <- a %in% c("gdfix", "sgdls", "mom", "adam")
    req(!fixed || !is.null(input[[paste0("lr", s)]]))
    run_alg(a, theta0(), D$x, D$y, as.numeric(input$maxit),
            tol = if (is.null(input$gtol)) 1e-6 else as.numeric(input$gtol),
            patience = if (is.null(input$stall)) Inf else as.numeric(input$stall),
            lr  = if (fixed) as.numeric(input[[paste0("lr", s)]]) else NA,
            mom = if (a == "mom") input[[paste0("mom", s)]] else NA,
            m   = if (a %in% MINIBATCH) as.numeric(input[[paste0("batch", s)]]) else NA)
  })
  runA <- mkrun("A"); runB <- mkrun("B")
  ## the network panels show the run chosen in "Network of"
  netsel <- reactive(if (identical(input$netsel, "B") && !is.null(runB())) "B" else "A")
  run <- reactive(if (netsel() == "B") runB() else runA())

  ## the browser owns the iteration (slider, play timer, buttons); a new run restarts it
  observeEvent(list(runA(), runB()), {
    nmax <- max(runA()$n, if (is.null(runB())) 0L else runB()$n)
    session$sendCustomMessage("krun", list(max = nmax - 1L,
                                           play = isTRUE(input$autoplay) && nmax > 1))
  })
  kraw <- reactive(as.integer(if (is.null(input$kshow)) 0L else input$kshow))
  kpos <- reactive(min(kraw(), run()$n - 1L))

  cur <- reactive({
    R <- run(); k <- min(kpos(), R$n - 1L) + 1L
    list(R = R, k = k, th = R$P[k, ], g = R$G[k, ])
  })

  output$netv <- renderPlot({
    C <- cur(); R <- C$R
    vmax <- max(3, quantile(abs(R$P), 0.95))
    par(mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1))
    draw_net(C$th, vmax, as.numeric(input$ctr),
             sprintf("%s: weights, iteration %d   (loss %.4f)", netsel(), C$k - 1L, R$F[C$k]))
  })

  output$netg <- renderPlot({
    C <- cur()
    gmax <- max(1e-8, max(abs(C$g)))
    par(mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1))
    draw_net(C$g, gmax, as.numeric(input$ctr),
             sprintf("%s: gradient of the loss, iteration %d", netsel(), C$k - 1L),
             arrows = FALSE, digits = 3)
  })

  ## one clearly different colour per hidden unit
  PCOL <- c("#F28E00", "#1F5FBF", "black", "#00B5CC")

  output$fit <- renderPlot({
    RA <- runA(); RB <- runB(); R <- RA; D <- DAT(); kk <- kraw()
    xg <- seq(-3, 3, length.out = 300) * xsc()
    par(mar = c(4, 4.2, 2.5, 1))
    plot(D$x, D$yj, pch = 19, cex = 0.7,
         col = adjustcolor("#E8820C", 0.5), ylim = c(0, max(D$y) + 1),
         xlab = "x", ylab = expression(lambda(x) ~ "and counts y"),
         main = "fitted mean and the generated data")
    lines(xg, lambda_fun(TT(), xg), col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)
    lines(xg, lambda_fun(R$P[1, ], xg), col = "grey60", lwd = 2)
    lines(xg, lambda_fun(RA$P[min(kk, RA$n - 1L) + 1L, ], xg), col = "#2E8B57", lwd = 3)
    if (!is.null(RB))
      lines(xg, lambda_fun(RB$P[min(kk, RB$n - 1L) + 1L, ], xg), col = "#1F5FBF", lwd = 2.5)
    leg <- data.frame(
      lab = c("true mean", "starting weights", paste("A:", alg_name(input$algA)), "counts"),
      lwd = c(2, 2, 3, NA), lty = c(2, 1, 1, NA), pch = c(NA, NA, NA, 19),
      col = c("red", "grey60", "#2E8B57", adjustcolor("#E8820C", 0.7)),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    if (!is.null(RB))
      leg <- rbind(leg, data.frame(lab = paste("B:", alg_name(input$algB)), lwd = 2.5, lty = 1,
                                   pch = NA, col = "#1F5FBF", stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
    legend("topright", bty = "n", cex = 0.78, lwd = leg$lwd, lty = leg$lty,
           pch = leg$pch, col = leg$col, legend = leg$lab)
  })

  ## the same fit on the log scale, where the units simply add up
  output$eta <- renderPlot({
    C <- cur(); xg <- seq(-3, 3, length.out = 300) * xsc()
    VH <- unit_terms(C$th, xg)
    eta <- C$th[3 * J + 1] + rowSums(VH)
    eta_true <- log(lambda_fun(TT(), xg))
    par(mar = c(4, 4.2, 2.5, 1))
    matplot(xg, VH, type = "l", lty = 3, lwd = 2.5, col = PCOL,
            ylim = pmax(-8, pmin(8, range(VH, eta, eta_true))),
            xlab = "x", ylab = expression(log ~ lambda(x)),
            main = "log scale: the scaled units v_j h_j add up to the fit")
    abline(h = 0, lty = 3, col = "grey70")
    lines(xg, eta_true, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)
    lines(xg, eta, col = "#2E8B57", lwd = 3)
    legend("topright", bty = "n", cex = 0.78, ncol = 2,
           lwd = c(rep(2.5, J), 3, 2), lty = c(rep(3, J), 1, 2),
           col = c(PCOL, "#2E8B57", "red"),
           legend = c(paste0("v", 1:J, " h", 1:J), "sum + v0 (fit)", "true"))
  })

  output$conv <- renderPlot({
    R <- runA(); RF <- runB(); C <- list(R = R, k = min(kraw(), R$n - 1L) + 1L)
    it <- 0:(R$n - 1)
    gn <- sqrt(rowSums(R$G^2))
    par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4.2, 2.5, 1))
    xl <- c(0, max(R$n, if (is.null(RF)) 0 else RF$n) - 1)
    ## the loss on the scale chosen below: as is, its log10, or the log10 of its excess
    ## over the smallest value either run reaches (so differences near the floor show)
    sc <- if (is.null(input$lscale)) "log" else input$lscale
    best <- min(c(R$F, RF$F), na.rm = TRUE)
    ls_fun <- function(v) switch(sc, lin = v, log = log10(pmax(v, 1e-12)),
                                 exc = log10(pmax(v - best, 1e-12)))
    ls_lab <- switch(sc, lin = "loss", log = expression(log[10] ~ "loss"),
                     exc = expression(log[10] ~ "(loss - smallest reached)"))
    plot(it, ls_fun(R$F), type = "b", pch = 20, col = "#2E8B57", xlab = "iteration",
         ylab = ls_lab, xlim = xl, ylim = range(c(ls_fun(R$F), ls_fun(RF$F)), finite = TRUE),
         main = "average negative log-likelihood")
    if (!is.null(RF)) {
      lines(0:(RF$n - 1), ls_fun(RF$F), type = "b", pch = 20, col = "#1F5FBF")
      kb <- min(kraw(), RF$n - 1L)
      points(kb, ls_fun(RF$F[kb + 1L]), pch = 19, col = "#1F5FBF", cex = 1.6)
      legend("topright", bty = "n", cex = 0.8, lty = 1, pch = 20,
             col = c("#2E8B57", "#1F5FBF"),
             legend = c(paste("A:", alg_name(input$algA)), paste("B:", alg_name(input$algB))))
    }
    points(it[C$k], ls_fun(R$F[C$k]), pch = 19, col = "#2E8B57", cex = 1.6)
    gnr <- if (is.null(RF)) NULL else log10(sqrt(rowSums(RF$G^2)))
    plot(it, log10(gn), type = "b", pch = 20, col = "#2E8B57", xlab = "iteration",
         xlim = xl, ylim = range(c(log10(gn), gnr), finite = TRUE),
         ylab = expression(log[10] ~ "||gradient||"), main = "gradient norm")
    if (!is.null(RF)) {
      lines(0:(RF$n - 1), gnr, type = "b", pch = 20, col = "#1F5FBF")
      points(kb, gnr[kb + 1L], pch = 19, col = "#1F5FBF", cex = 1.6)
    }
    points(it[C$k], log10(gn[C$k]), pch = 19, col = "#2E8B57", cex = 1.6)
  })

  output$info <- renderUI({
    D <- DAT(); kk <- kraw()
    line <- function(R, a, tag, col) {
      k <- min(kk, R$n - 1L) + 1L; al <- R$A[k]
      paste0("<b style='color:", col, "'>", tag, ": ", alg_name(a), "</b> &nbsp; <b>",
             if (a %in% MINIBATCH) "epoch" else "iteration", "</b> ", k - 1L, " of ", R$n - 1L,
             " &nbsp; <b>loss</b> ", formatC(R$F[k], digits = 5, format = "f"),
             " &nbsp; <b>||gradient||</b> ", formatC(sqrt(sum(R$G[k, ]^2)), digits = 3, format = "g"),
             if (is.finite(al)) paste0(" &nbsp; <b>",
                                       if (a %in% c("gdfix", "mom", "adam")) "learning rate"
                                       else "step length", "</b> ",
                                       formatC(al, digits = 3, format = "g")) else "",
             "<br><i>", R$note, "</i>")
    }
    HTML(paste(line(runA(), input$algA, "A", "#2E8B57"),
               if (!is.null(runB())) line(runB(), input$algB, "B", "#1F5FBF"),
               sep = "<br>"))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

## About the app

Fits a Poisson neural network like the one in the book's backpropagation section, with one covariate and four `tanh` hidden units, to counts generated from known weights, and lets you watch seven optimizers work on it: gradient descent with a fixed learning rate, gradient descent with a line search, conjugate gradient and BFGS, which use the full data, and SGD with a line search, SGD with momentum and SGD with Adam, which step through mini-batches. The four units are enough for a mean with two modes: the true weights switch units 1 and 2 on and off around $x \in (-2.2, -0.8)$, and units 3 and 4 around $(0.8, 2.2)$.

**The weights.** The network panels belong to one optimizer, chosen by **Network of** above them. The upper network shows the thirteen weights at the current iteration. The eight weights on edges (`w11, …, w41` from $x$ to the hidden units and `v1, …, v4` from the hidden units to the output) are written on their edges, and each intercept (`w10, …, w40` and `v0`) is a node of its own, a box hung on the neuron it shifts. Colour shows the value (blue negative, red positive; on an edge it also sets the width). The arrows beside a value change that weight (up and down on an edge, right to increase and left to decrease on an intercept box), and the starting point of the run changes with it. **True Value** loads the weights that generated the data, **Random** draws a new set (for the scaled predictor, drawn for $x$ divided by the scale), and **Zero** sets every weight to 0 (a saddle point of the loss: with all hidden weights at zero, only $v_0$ has a nonzero gradient). **Adjust Size** sets how much one click on an arrow changes a weight.

**The methods.** Write $g_k = \nabla L(\theta_k)$ for the gradient of the average loss $L$ over all $n$ observations at the current weights, $\ell_i$ for the loss of observation $i$, and $g_k^{(B_k)} = \frac{1}{m}\sum_{i \in B_k} \nabla \ell_i(\theta_k)$ for the gradient of the mini-batch $B_k$ of $m$ observations used at update $k$ (the superscript names the batch, the subscript the iteration). The first four optimizers in the menu use the full data; the last three step through mini-batches. All of them can be written as one update

$$\theta_{k+1} = \theta_k - \alpha_k\, P_k\, m_k ,$$

where $m_k$ is the gradient actually used (the full gradient, a mini-batch gradient, or an average of past ones), $P_k$ is a *preconditioner* that rescales or rotates the step, and $\alpha_k$ is the step size.

| Optimizer | Gradient used, $m_k$ | Preconditioner, $P_k$ | Step size, $\alpha_k$ |
|:------------|:------------------------|:-------------------|:-----------------|
| **GD, fixed rate** | $g_k$ | $I$ | $\alpha$, set by hand |
| **GD + line search** | $g_k$ | $I$ | $\alpha_k$ from a Wolfe line search |
| **Conjugate gradient (PR+)** | $d_k = -g_k + \beta_k d_{k-1}$, with $\beta_k = \max\!\Big(0, \dfrac{g_k^\top (g_k - g_{k-1})}{g_{k-1}^\top g_{k-1}}\Big)$ | implicit: the new gradient is combined with the previous direction | $\alpha_k$ from a Wolfe line search |
| **BFGS** | $g_k$ | $B_k \approx H^{-1}$, a full matrix, updated by $B_{k+1} = (I - \rho\, s y^\top) B_k (I - \rho\, y s^\top) + \rho\, s s^\top$ with $s = \theta_{k+1} - \theta_k$, $y = g_{k+1} - g_k$, $\rho = 1/(s^\top y)$ | $\alpha_k$ from a Wolfe line search |
| **SGD + line search** | $g_k^{(B_k)}$, with $E\,g_k^{(B_k)} = g_k$ | $I$ | $\alpha_k$ by backtracking on the loss of the mini-batch $B_k$: start at the learning rate and halve until $L^{(B_k)}(\theta_k - \alpha g_k^{(B_k)}) \le L^{(B_k)}(\theta_k) - c_1 \alpha \|g_k^{(B_k)}\|^2$ |
| **SGD + momentum** | $v_k = \mu\, v_{k-1} + g_k^{(B_k)}$, an exponentially weighted sum of past mini-batch gradients | $I$ | $\alpha$, set by hand |
| **SGD + Adam** | $\hat m_k = \dfrac{(1-\beta_1)\sum_{j \le k} \beta_1^{k-j} g_j^{(B_j)}}{1-\beta_1^{k}}$, a bias-corrected average of past mini-batch gradients | $\mathrm{diag}\big(1/(\sqrt{\hat v_k} + \epsilon)\big)$, with $\hat v_k = \dfrac{(1-\beta_2)\sum_{j \le k} \beta_2^{k-j} g_j^{(B_j)} \odot g_j^{(B_j)}}{1-\beta_2^{k}}$ | $\alpha$, set by hand |

In the app $\beta_1 = 0.9$, $\beta_2 = 0.999$ and $\epsilon = 10^{-8}$ for Adam, and $k$ counts mini-batch updates. Momentum is coded as $v \leftarrow \mu v - \alpha g^{(B)}$, $\theta \leftarrow \theta + v$, the same update written with the sign and $\alpha$ absorbed into $v$. A Wolfe line search takes the step $\alpha$ along $d_k = -P_k m_k$ that satisfies both $L(\theta_k + \alpha d_k) \le L(\theta_k) + c_1 \alpha\, g_k^\top d_k$ (sufficient decrease) and $\nabla L(\theta_k + \alpha d_k)^\top d_k \ge c_2\, g_k^\top d_k$ (curvature), with $c_1 = 10^{-4}$ and $c_2 = 0.9$.

*What each one changes.* Fixed-rate GD and the line-search methods use the exact gradient. A line search removes the learning rate to tune; conjugate gradient and BFGS also change the direction, CG by combining the gradient with the previous direction and BFGS by learning an approximation of the inverse Hessian from gradient differences, the only full-matrix preconditioner here (compare Newton's method, $P_k = H^{-1}$). The three SGD methods replace the gradient by a cheap and noisy mini-batch gradient. SGD with a line search chooses each step by backtracking on the loss of the batch itself, so the step is adapted to the batch and not to the whole loss. Momentum averages the mini-batch gradients, which damps their noise and the zig-zag across a valley. Adam also divides each coordinate by the square root of a running average of its squared gradients, a per-coordinate step size; why this helps so much is not fully understood (see the book's discussion).

*When a run stops.* A run ends at the first of: the full-data gradient norm falls below the tolerance in **Stop: ||g|| <**; if **Stop if flat for** is set, the full-data loss has not improved by 0.001% in that many consecutive iterations (a patience rule, off by default, the only kind that can stop a noisy method, whose gradient norm never gets small; it also ends a method that has stalled on a plateau, so read the message in the info line); or the maximum number of iterations. The info line says which one applied. A mini-batch run is also capped at 100000 mini-batch updates, which it reports. A conjugate-gradient or BFGS run whose line search fails first restarts from steepest descent, and ends only if that fails too.

*Epochs and mini-batches.* For the three SGD methods one iteration is one *epoch*: a shuffled pass of $\lceil n/m \rceil$ mini-batch updates over all the data. An iteration therefore costs about as many gradient evaluations as one full-batch step of the other methods, and the iteration axes are directly comparable. This is the point of the comparison. After the same number of passes through the data, the mini-batch methods have made $n/m$ updates per pass where gradient descent has made one, so on a large sample they are well ahead of a full-batch method such as **GD + line search** in the plots. With the batch size equal to $n$ the three methods use the full gradient. The loss and gradient norm shown are always those of the full data. The sample size goes up to 2000: the larger $n$ is, the more mini-batch updates an epoch holds ($n/m$), and the clearer the advantage over the full-batch methods becomes. For these thirteen parameters and a small sample, BFGS is hard to beat; SGD, momentum and Adam are what larger networks use, where a Hessian approximation is too expensive and a pass through all the data is rarely made. To keep the browser responsive a mini-batch run stops after 100000 updates in all, which the info line reports.

**Scale of $x$.** The predictor is multiplied by this factor and the slope weights of the generating network are divided by it, so the true curve is the same function of $x$ divided by the scale and only the parameterization changes. The gradient with respect to a slope weight $w_{j1}$ carries a factor $x$ and the gradient with respect to an intercept does not, so a scale far from 1 makes the gradients of the weights differ by orders of magnitude. A single learning rate is then right for some weights and wrong for others: fixed-rate GD and momentum must shrink it to suit the most sensitive weight, which makes the other weights crawl, while Adam, which rescales each weight separately, needs a smaller change. When the scale changes, the app resets each learning rate to a value divided by $s^2$ for fixed-rate GD, SGD and momentum (the curvature in a slope weight grows like $s^2$) and by $s$ for Adam (its step is measured in the weight itself, which shrinks like $1/s$); raise the rate again to see the instability, and use **True Value** as the start to see the noise of the mini-batch methods around a good fit. The line-search methods are less sensitive, because the step length adapts, but BFGS and CG slow down when the problem is badly scaled. Changing the scale restarts the run.

**The gradient.** The lower network has the same layout, with each edge and intercept box coloured by the corresponding component of the gradient of the loss, computed by backpropagation. Its colour scale is set by the largest component at the current iteration, so you can see which weights the method is still pushing on as the run converges.

**The fit.** The right panel shows the generated counts, the true mean curve (dashed red, with its two modes), the mean curve at the starting weights (grey) and the current fit (green). Two optimizers, **A** (green) and **B** (blue, or *None*), are run from the same start on the same data, each with its own settings, and both fits are drawn at the same iteration, so any two of the methods can be compared; the loss and gradient-norm plots show both paths. The default pair is SGD with Adam against gradient descent with a line search, which shows what the mini-batch updates buy per pass through the data. Because $\log\lambda = v_0 + \sum_j v_j h_j$, the units combine by adding in the exponent, not by adding curves, so the second plot shows the fit on the log scale: the four scaled units $v_j h_j$ (dotted; orange, blue, black and cyan for units 1 to 4) simply add up to $\log\lambda$ (green), and the true $\log\lambda$ (dashed red) is the target. The box above the plots hides this second plot. Beneath the fit are the loss and the gradient norm per iteration. The loss plot is on a log10 scale by default, since the loss is often close to its floor and the methods differ only in the last digits; the buttons under it switch to the loss itself, or to the log of the loss minus the smallest value either run reaches, which makes the rate of convergence readable. The first row of controls sets up the data (sample size and a new dataset); the next two rows choose optimizers A and B and the settings of each (learning rate, momentum, mini-batch size); the last row holds the maximum number of iterations, the colour contrast, the playback buttons, and a slider that shows the fit at any iteration of the run (it follows the playback, and you can drag it to scrub through the run). The loss is not convex, so different starts can end at different fits; try **Random** a few times.

A Gaussian version of this app, for regression with normal noise, is [Fitting a Gaussian Neural Network by Gradient Methods](app_sgd.html).

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="R source for this app"}

````r
library(shiny)

## ------------------------------------------------------------------- model
## One covariate x, four tanh hidden units, log link, Poisson counts:
##   a_j = w_j1 x + w_j0,  h_j = tanh(a_j),  eta = v_0 + sum_j v_j h_j,
##   lambda = exp(eta).
## theta = (w11..wJ1,  w10..wJ0,  v1..vJ,  v0)
J <- 4
NP <- 3 * J + 1                                  # number of weights
NAMES <- c(paste0("w", 1:J, "1"), paste0("w", 1:J, "0"), paste0("v", 1:J), "v0")
BIASIDX <- c(J + 1:J, NP)                        # the intercepts w_j0 and v_0
## two bumps in the mean: units 1, 2 switch on and off over (-2.2, -0.8),
## units 3, 4 over (0.8, 2.2), so lambda(x) has two modes
TRUE_THETA <- c(2.5, 2.5, 2.5, 2.5,   5.5, 2, -2, -5.5,   1.2, -1.2, 1.0, -1.0,   -0.5)

fwd <- function(th, x) {
  H <- tanh(outer(x, th[1:J]) + rep(th[J + 1:J], each = length(x)))
  list(H = H, eta = as.vector(th[3 * J + 1] + H %*% th[2 * J + 1:J]))
}
lambda_fun <- function(th, x) exp(fwd(th, x)$eta)

## the scaled units v_j h_j(x), one column per hidden unit
unit_terms <- function(th, x) sweep(fwd(th, x)$H, 2, th[2 * J + 1:J], "*")

## average Poisson negative log-likelihood (the log y! term dropped)
nll <- function(th, x, y) {
  e <- fwd(th, x)$eta
  v <- mean(exp(e) - y * e)
  if (is.finite(v)) v else Inf
}

## its gradient by backpropagation:  delta_eta -> delta_a -> weights
nll_grad <- function(th, x, y) {
  E <- fwd(th, x)
  d_eta <- exp(E$eta) - y                                   # n
  d_a   <- (1 - E$H^2) * outer(d_eta, th[2 * J + 1:J])      # n x J
  c(colSums(d_a * x),                                       # w_j1
    colSums(d_a),                                           # w_j0
    as.vector(crossprod(E$H, d_eta)),                       # v_j
    sum(d_eta)) / length(x)                                 # v_0
}

make_data <- function(n, seed) {
  set.seed(100 + seed)
  x <- runif(n, -3, 3)
  y <- rpois(n, lambda_fun(TRUE_THETA, x))
  ## a fixed vertical offset, drawn once with the data, so the points stay put
  list(x = x, y = y, yj = y + runif(n, -0.12, 0.12))
}

rand_start <- function(seed) {
  set.seed(2000 + seed)
  c(rnorm(3 * J, 0, 1), 0)
}

## ------------------------------------------------------- Wolfe line search
line_search <- function(f, g, x, d, a0 = 1, c1 = 1e-4, c2 = 0.9) {
  f0 <- f(x); gd0 <- sum(g(x) * d)
  if (!is.finite(gd0) || gd0 >= 0) return(list(alpha = 0, ok = FALSE))
  lo <- 0; hi <- Inf; a <- a0
  for (it in 1:60) {
    fa <- f(x + a * d)
    if (!is.finite(fa) || fa > f0 + c1 * a * gd0) {
      hi <- a; a <- 0.5 * (lo + hi)
    } else {
      if (sum(g(x + a * d) * d) < c2 * gd0) {
        lo <- a
        a <- if (is.finite(hi)) 0.5 * (lo + hi) else min(2 * a, 1e4)
      } else {
        return(list(alpha = a, ok = TRUE))
      }
    }
    if (a < 1e-14) return(list(alpha = 0, ok = FALSE))
  }
  list(alpha = a, ok = (a > 0))
}

## ------------------------------------------------------------- algorithms
## the methods that step through mini-batches: one iteration is one epoch
MINIBATCH <- c("sgdls", "mom", "adam")
## Row k of P, G, F is the state after k - 1 steps; A[k] is the step length
## that led to it.
run_alg <- function(alg, th0, x, y, maxit, lr = 0.1, mom = 0.9, m = 20,
                    tol = 1e-6, patience = Inf, rtol = 1e-5) {
  p <- length(th0)
  f <- function(th) nll(th, x, y)
  g <- function(th) nll_grad(th, x, y)
  P <- G <- matrix(NA_real_, maxit + 1, p)
  Fv <- AL <- rep(NA_real_, maxit + 1)
  th <- th0; B <- diag(p)
  g_prev <- d_prev <- s_prev <- NULL
  n <- 0; note <- "maximum number of iterations reached"
  best_f <- Inf; best_k <- 1                  # the best loss so far, and when it was reached
  ## state for the fixed-rate rules
  n_obs <- length(x); m <- max(1, min(m, n_obs))
  capped <- FALSE
  if (alg %in% MINIBATCH) {                  # keep the number of mini-batch steps in check
    cap <- max(1, floor(100000 / ceiling(n_obs / m)))
    if (maxit > cap) { maxit <- cap; capped <- TRUE }
  }
  vel <- m1 <- m2 <- numeric(p)              # momentum velocity; Adam moments
  tt <- 0                                    # mini-batch updates so far (Adam)
  if (alg %in% MINIBATCH) set.seed(11)

  for (k in 1:(maxit + 1)) {
    gk <- g(th); fk <- f(th)
    P[k, ] <- th; G[k, ] <- gk; Fv[k] <- fk; n <- k
    if (!is.finite(fk) || !all(is.finite(gk))) { note <- "diverged"; break }
    if (tol > 0 && sqrt(sum(gk^2)) < tol) {
      note <- paste0("converged: gradient norm < ", format(tol)); break
    }
    ## no stopping rule can be exact for a noisy method, so every method also stops when the
    ## full-data loss has not improved by a fraction rtol for `patience` iterations
    if (k == 1 || fk < best_f - rtol * abs(best_f)) { best_f <- fk; best_k <- k }
    if (k - best_k >= patience) {
      note <- paste0("stopped: the loss has not improved by ", 100 * rtol, "% in ",
                     patience, " iterations"); break
    }
    if (k > maxit) break

    if (alg == "gdfix") {                    # full-batch gradient, fixed learning rate
      AL[k + 1] <- lr
      th <- th - lr * gk
      next
    }

    if (alg %in% MINIBATCH) {                # one iteration is one epoch: a shuffled pass
      perm <- sample.int(n_obs)              # of mini-batch steps over all the data, so
      al <- numeric(0)                       # it costs about one full-batch gradient
      for (s0 in seq(1, n_obs, by = m)) {
        idx <- perm[s0:min(s0 + m - 1, n_obs)]
        xb <- x[idx]; yb <- y[idx]
        gb <- nll_grad(th, xb, yb)               # the gradient of mini-batch B_k
        if (alg == "sgdls") {                # backtracking line search on the batch loss
          fb <- nll(th, xb, yb); a <- lr; gg <- sum(gb^2)
          for (j in 1:30) {
            fa <- nll(th - a * gb, xb, yb)
            if (is.finite(fa) && fa <= fb - 1e-4 * a * gg) break
            a <- a / 2
          }
          al <- c(al, a)
          th <- th - a * gb
        } else if (alg == "mom") {           # heavy ball on the batch gradient
          vel <- mom * vel - lr * gb
          th <- th + vel
        } else {                             # Adam on the batch gradient
          tt <- tt + 1
          m1 <- 0.9 * m1 + 0.1 * gb
          m2 <- 0.999 * m2 + 0.001 * gb^2
          th <- th - lr * (m1 / (1 - 0.9^tt)) / (sqrt(m2 / (1 - 0.999^tt)) + 1e-8)
        }
      }
      AL[k + 1] <- if (alg == "sgdls") mean(al) else lr
      next
    }

    if (alg == "gd") {
      d <- -gk
    } else if (alg == "cg") {
      if (is.null(d_prev)) {
        d <- -gk
      } else {
        yk <- gk - g_prev
        beta <- max(0, sum(gk * yk) / max(sum(g_prev^2), 1e-300))   # PR+
        d <- -gk + beta * d_prev
      }
      if (sum(gk * d) > -1e-12) d <- -gk                           # restart
    } else {                                                       # BFGS
      if (!is.null(s_prev)) {
        yk <- gk - g_prev; sy <- sum(s_prev * yk)
        if (sy > 1e-10) {
          if (k == 2) B <- (sy / sum(yk^2)) * diag(p)    # scale the first B
          rho <- 1 / sy
          V <- diag(p) - rho * outer(s_prev, yk)
          B <- V %*% B %*% t(V) + rho * outer(s_prev, s_prev)
        }
      }
      d <- -as.vector(B %*% gk)
      if (sum(gk * d) > -1e-12) { B <- diag(p); d <- -gk }
    }

    a0 <- if (alg == "bfgs" && k > 1) 1 else min(1, 1 / sqrt(sum(d^2)))
    ls <- line_search(f, g, th, d, a0)
    if (!ls$ok && alg != "gd") {             # restart from steepest descent before giving up
      d <- -gk; B <- diag(p); d_prev <- s_prev <- g_prev <- NULL
      ls <- line_search(f, g, th, d, min(1, 1 / sqrt(sum(d^2))))
    }
    if (!ls$ok) { note <- "line search failed"; break }
    AL[k + 1] <- ls$alpha
    s_prev <- ls$alpha * d; g_prev <- gk; d_prev <- d
    th <- th + s_prev
  }
  if (capped && grepl("^maximum", note))
    note <- paste0("stopped after ", maxit, " epochs (100000 mini-batch steps)")
  i <- seq_len(n)
  list(P = P[i, , drop = FALSE], G = G[i, , drop = FALSE], F = Fv[i],
       A = AL[i], n = n, note = note)
}

ALGS <- c("Gradient descent, fixed learning rate"     = "gdfix",
          "Gradient descent + line search"            = "gd",
          "Conjugate gradient (Polak-Ribiere+)"       = "cg",
          "BFGS (quasi-Newton)"                       = "bfgs",
          "SGD + line search (on each mini-batch)"    = "sgdls",
          "SGD + momentum"                            = "mom",
          "SGD + Adam"                                = "adam")

alg_name <- function(a) if (a == "none") "none" else names(ALGS)[ALGS == a]

## --------------------------------------------------------- network layout
## Weights sit on the edges; each intercept is a node of its own, a box with
## the value and its arrows, hung on the neuron it shifts.
NX <- c(0.07, 0.50)                                 # (x, y) of the input node
YH <- seq(0.88, 0.12, length.out = J); XH <- 0.60   # hidden nodes
NO <- c(1.13, 0.50)                                 # output node
at <- function(p, q, f) p + f * (q - p)             # a point along an edge
## hidden intercepts hang above the upper half of the hidden nodes and below the rest
YB <- YH + rep(c(0.14, -0.14), each = J / 2)
BIAS <- c(rep(0.56, J), 1.00)                       # x of the intercept boxes
BIASY <- c(YB, 0.17)                                # y of the intercept boxes
## where each weight's value and arrows sit
ADJ <- local({
  hj <- lapply(1:J, function(j) c(XH, YH[j]))
  pos <- c(lapply(1:J, function(j) at(NX, hj[[j]], 0.50)),    # w_j1: x -> h_j
           lapply(1:J, function(j) c(BIAS[j], BIASY[j])),     # w_j0: box on h_j
           lapply(1:J, function(j) at(hj[[j]], NO, 0.50)),    # v_j: h_j -> out
           list(c(BIAS[J + 1], BIASY[J + 1])))                # v_0: box on output
  data.frame(idx = 1:NP, sym = NAMES,
             x = sapply(pos, `[`, 1), y = sapply(pos, `[`, 2),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
})
## the arrows beside each value (also the click targets): up / down beside an
## edge weight, left / right beside an intercept box
AX <- 0.104                                  # arrow offset from the value
isb <- ADJ$idx %in% BIASIDX
ARROWS <- rbind(
  data.frame(idx = ADJ$idx, dir = +1, horiz = isb,
             ax = ifelse(isb, ADJ$x + AX, ADJ$x + AX),
             ay = ifelse(isb, ADJ$y, ADJ$y + 0.028)),
  data.frame(idx = ADJ$idx, dir = -1, horiz = isb,
             ax = ifelse(isb, ADJ$x - AX, ADJ$x + AX),
             ay = ifelse(isb, ADJ$y, ADJ$y - 0.028)))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------- colours
## Diverging ramp: blue = negative, red = positive, depth by magnitude.
DIV <- colorRampPalette(c("#08306B", "#2171B5", "#6BAED6", "#DEEBF7",
                          "#F7F7F7",
                          "#FEE0D2", "#FC9272", "#CB181D", "#67000D"))(201)

## compander: maps v in [-vmax, vmax] to [-1, 1], boosting small values
tone <- function(v, vmax, k) {
  u <- pmax(-1, pmin(1, v / vmax))
  sign(u) * log1p(k * abs(u)) / log1p(k)
}
hcol <- function(v, vmax, k) DIV[round((tone(v, vmax, k) + 1) * 100) + 1]

draw_net <- function(v, vmax, k, main, arrows = TRUE, digits = 2) {
  col <- hcol(v, vmax, k); lw <- 0.8 + 6 * abs(tone(v, vmax, k))
  plot.new(); plot.window(c(0, 1.2), c(-0.25, 1.08))
  title(main = main, cex.main = 1.05)
  H <- cbind(XH, YH)
  ## edges, each carrying one weight: x -> h_j (w_j1), h_j -> output (v_j)
  for (j in 1:J) {
    segments(NX[1], NX[2], H[j, 1], H[j, 2], col = col[j],     lwd = lw[j],     lend = 1)
    segments(H[j, 1], H[j, 2], NO[1], NO[2], col = col[2 * J + j], lwd = lw[2 * J + j], lend = 1)
  }
  ## intercept nodes: a thin arrow from each box to the neuron it shifts
  tgt <- rbind(H, NO)
  for (i in seq_along(BIASIDX)) {
    b <- ADJ[BIASIDX[i], ]
    dy <- sign(tgt[i, 2] - b$y)
    if (i == J + 1) arrows(b$x, b$y + 0.03, NO[1] - 0.03, NO[2] - 0.03, length = 0.08,
                       col = "grey45", lwd = 1.4)
    else arrows(b$x, b$y + dy * 0.035, tgt[i, 1], tgt[i, 2] - dy * 0.035,
                length = 0.08, col = "grey45", lwd = 1.4)
  }
  ## nodes
  points(rbind(NX, H, NO), pch = 21, cex = 3.2, bg = "white", lwd = 1.6)
  text(NX[1], NX[2], "x", font = 2)
  text(H[, 1], H[, 2], paste0("h", 1:J), cex = 0.8)
  text(NO[1], NO[2], expression(lambda), cex = 1.1)
  ## values: an intercept is a box coloured by its value; an edge weight is
  ## plain text on a white patch so the edge does not strike through it
  for (i in 1:NP) {
    b <- ADJ[i, ]; isb <- i %in% BIASIDX
    if (isb) rect(b$x - 0.075, b$y - 0.036, b$x + 0.075, b$y + 0.036,
                  col = col[i], border = "grey35")
    else rect(b$x - 0.072, b$y - 0.028, b$x + 0.072, b$y + 0.028,
              col = adjustcolor("white", 0.8), border = NA)
    dark <- abs(tone(v[i], vmax, k)) > 0.62
    text(b$x, b$y, sprintf(paste0("%s=%.", digits, "f"), b$sym, v[i]),
         cex = 0.85, font = if (isb) 1 else 2,
         col = if (isb) { if (dark) "white" else "black" }
               else if (dark) col[i] else "grey20")
  }
  if (arrows) for (r in seq_len(nrow(ARROWS))) {
    a <- ARROWS[r, ]
    if (a$horiz)                                   # left / right: -, +
      polygon(a$ax + a$dir * c(-0.013, -0.013, 0.015),
              a$ay + c(-0.033, 0.033, 0), col = "grey30", border = NA)
    else                                           # down / up: -, +
      polygon(a$ax + c(-0.026, 0.026, 0), a$ay + a$dir * c(-0.016, -0.016, 0.02),
              col = "grey30", border = NA)
  }
  ## signed colour bar
  xs <- seq(0.12, 1.08, length.out = 201)
  rect(xs, -0.24, xs + diff(xs)[1], -0.19, col = DIV, border = NA)
  lab <- formatC(vmax, format = "g", digits = 2)
  text(c(0.12, 0.60, 1.08), -0.16, c(paste0("-", lab), "0", paste0("+", lab)),
       cex = 0.72)
}

## --------------------------------------------------------------------- UI
## an icon-only playback button; the title shows as a tooltip
ctrl_btn <- function(id, icon_name, title, class = "btn-default")
  actionButton(id, NULL, icon = icon(icon_name), title = title, class = class,
               style = "flex: 1; padding: 6px 0;")

row_label <- function(txt)
  column(1, div(style = "padding-top: 28px;", tags$b(txt)))

## learning rates on a roughly logarithmic grid (rates need to range over orders of magnitude)
LRGRID <- c(1e-5, 3e-5, 1e-4, 3e-4, 1e-3, 3e-3, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1)
LRCHOICES <- setNames(as.character(LRGRID), format(LRGRID, scientific = FALSE, drop0trailing = TRUE))

## one optimizer: its menu, then the parameters that belong to the chosen method
opt_row <- function(s, selected, col, none = FALSE) {
  a <- paste0("input.alg", s)
  has_lr <- paste0("['gdfix', 'sgdls', 'mom', 'adam'].indexOf(", a, ") >= 0")
  has_b  <- paste0("['sgdls', 'mom', 'adam'].indexOf(", a, ") >= 0")
  fluidRow(
    column(1, div(style = paste0("padding-top: 28px; font-size: 20px; color: ", col, ";"),
                  tags$b(s))),
    column(3, selectInput(paste0("alg", s), "Optimizer",
                          choices = if (none) c("None" = "none", ALGS) else ALGS,
                          selected = selected, width = "100%")),
    column(8,
      conditionalPanel(has_lr,
        div(class = "steprule",
          div(selectInput(paste0("lr", s), "Learning rate (first step if line search)",
                          choices = LRCHOICES, selected = "0.3", width = "100%")),
          conditionalPanel(paste0(a, " == 'mom'"),
            div(sliderInput(paste0("mom", s), "Momentum", min = 0, max = 0.99,
                            value = 0.9, step = 0.01, width = "100%"))),
          conditionalPanel(has_b,
            div(selectInput(paste0("batch", s), "Mini-batch size",
                            choices = c("5" = 5, "10" = 10, "20" = 20, "50" = 50,
                                        "100" = 100, "all n (full batch)" = 1e6),
                            selected = 20, width = "100%"))))),
      conditionalPanel(paste0(has_lr, " == false && ", a, " != 'none'"),
        div(style = "padding-top: 28px;",
            helpText("The step length comes from a Wolfe line search."))))
  )
}

ui <- fluidPage(
  ## the iteration slider is the only state: the browser moves it (play timer, buttons,
  ## dragging), and the server just reads input$kshow
  tags$head(tags$script(HTML("
    var ktimer = null, kdrag = false, kself = false, kuser = 0;
    function kcur() { return parseInt($('#kshow').val()); }
    function kslider() { return $('#kshow').data('ionRangeSlider'); }
    function kset(v) {
      var s = kslider(); if (!s) return;
      kself = true;
      s.update({from: Math.max(s.options.min, Math.min(s.options.max, v))});
      $('#kshow').trigger('change'); kself = false; }
    function kplay(on) {
      if (ktimer) { clearInterval(ktimer); ktimer = null; }
      $('#play i').removeClass('fa-play fa-pause').addClass(on ? 'fa-pause' : 'fa-play');
      if (!on) return;
      var s = kslider(); if (s && kcur() >= s.options.max) kset(0);
      ktimer = setInterval(function() {
        if (kdrag || Date.now() - kuser < 600) return;   // the user is on the slider
        var s = kslider();
        if (kcur() >= s.options.max) kplay(false); else kset(kcur() + 1);
      }, 300); }
    ['mousedown', 'touchstart', 'pointerdown'].forEach(function(ev) {
      document.addEventListener(ev, function(e) {
        if ($(e.target).closest('.shiny-input-container').find('#kshow').length) {
          kdrag = true; kuser = Date.now(); } }, true); });
    ['mouseup', 'touchend', 'pointerup'].forEach(function(ev) {
      document.addEventListener(ev, function() { kdrag = false; kuser = Date.now(); }, true); });
    $(document).on('change', '#kshow', function() { if (!kself) kuser = Date.now(); });
    $(document).on('click', '#play', function() { kplay(!ktimer); });
    $(document).on('click', '#step',  function() { kplay(false); kset(kcur() + 1); });
    $(document).on('click', '#back',  function() { kplay(false); kset(kcur() - 1); });
    $(document).on('click', '#first', function() { kplay(false); kset(0); });
    $(document).on('click', '#toend', function() { kplay(false); kset(kslider().options.max); });
    Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('krun', function(m) {
      kplay(false);
      var s = kslider(); if (s) { s.update({max: m.max, from: 0}); $('#kshow').trigger('change'); }
      if (m.play) kplay(true); });
  "))),
  ## small text for the row of weight buttons
  tags$head(tags$style(HTML("
    .wbar .btn { font-size: 12px; padding: 3px 10px; }
    .wbar label { font-size: 12px; margin-bottom: 1px; }
    .wbar .form-group { margin-bottom: 0; }
    .wbar .selectize-input, .wbar select { font-size: 12px; min-height: 26px;
                                           padding: 3px 8px; }
    .steprule { display: flex; gap: 14px; }
    .steprule > div { flex: 1; min-width: 0; }"))),
  ## ---- control panel, at the top -------------------------------------------
  wellPanel(
    ## the data
    fluidRow(
      row_label("Setup"),
      column(2, sliderInput("n", "Sample size n", min = 50, max = 2000,
                            value = 150, step = 50, width = "100%")),
      column(2, selectInput("xscale", "Scale of x", choices = c("0.1" = 0.1, "1" = 1, "10" = 10, "100" = 100),
                            selected = 1, width = "100%")),
      column(2, div(style = "padding-top: 25px;",
                    actionButton("newdata", "Regenerate data",
                                 class = "btn-warning", style = "width:100%;")))
    ),
    hr(style = "margin: 4px 0 8px;"),
    ## two optimizers, each with its own settings: A (green) and B (blue)
    opt_row("A", "adam", "#2E8B57"),
    opt_row("B", "gd", "#1F5FBF", none = TRUE),
    hr(style = "margin: 4px 0 8px;"),
    ## how long to run them, the colour scale, the play buttons, the iteration shown
    fluidRow(
      row_label("Run"),
      column(1, selectInput("maxit", "Max iterations",
                            choices = c(10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000),
                            selected = 100, width = "100%")),
      column(1, selectInput("ctr", "Contrast",
                            choices = c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32), selected = 8,
                            width = "100%")),
      column(1, selectInput("gtol", "Stop: ||g|| <",
                            choices = c("0.1" = 0.1, "0.01" = 0.01, "1e-3" = 0.001,
                                        "1e-4" = 1e-4, "1e-6" = 1e-6, "1e-8" = 1e-8,
                                        "never" = 0),
                            selected = 1e-6, width = "100%")),
      column(1, selectInput("stall", "Stop if flat for",
                            choices = c("never" = Inf, "100 its" = 100, "50 its" = 50, "20 its" = 20),
                            selected = Inf, width = "100%")),
      column(3, div(style = "display: flex; gap: 4px; padding-top: 22px;",
                    ctrl_btn("first", "backward-fast", "Back to the start"),
                    ctrl_btn("back",  "backward-step", "One iteration back"),
                    ctrl_btn("play",  "play",          "Play / pause",
                             class = "btn-primary"),
                    ctrl_btn("step",  "forward-step",  "One iteration forward"),
                    ctrl_btn("toend", "forward-fast",  "To the end")),
             checkboxInput("autoplay", "Autoplay on change", FALSE)),
      column(3, sliderInput("kshow", "Iteration shown", min = 0, max = 100,
                            value = 0, step = 1, width = "100%"))
    )
  ),  fluidRow(
    ## ---- left: the network of values above the network of gradients -----
    column(6,
      div(class = "wbar",
          style = "display: flex; gap: 6px; align-items: flex-end; margin-bottom: 4px;",
          actionButton("settrue", "True Value", class = "btn-success"),
          actionButton("newstart", "Random"),
          actionButton("setzero", "Zero"),
          div(style = "width: 110px; margin-left: 6px;",
              selectInput("astep", "Adjust Size",
                          choices = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1),
                          selected = 0.25, width = "100%")),
          div(style = "width: 90px; margin-left: 6px;",
              selectInput("netsel", "Network of", choices = c("A", "B"), width = "100%"))),
      plotOutput("netv", height = "420px", click = "netv_click"),
      plotOutput("netg", height = "420px"),
      helpText("Click the up / down arrows beside a weight to change the ",
               "starting value (this restarts the run). The true values are ",
               "those that generated the data.")),
    ## ---- right: the fitted mean, and how the optimizer is doing -----------
    column(6,
      checkboxInput("showparts", "Show the units on the log scale", TRUE),
      plotOutput("fit", height = "380px"),
      conditionalPanel("input.showparts", plotOutput("eta", height = "250px")),
      plotOutput("conv", height = "230px"),
      radioButtons("lscale", NULL, inline = TRUE,
                   choices = c("log10 loss" = "log", "log10 (loss - smallest reached)" = "exc",
                               "loss" = "lin")),
      htmlOutput("info"))
  )
)

## ----------------------------------------------------------------- server
server <- function(input, output, session) {

  dseed <- reactiveVal(1); rseed <- reactiveVal(1)
  theta0 <- reactiveVal(rand_start(1))        # the starting weights

  observeEvent(input$newdata, dseed(dseed() + 1))
  ## a sensible starting learning rate for each fixed-rate method
  ## a sensible learning rate for the method and the scale of x: the curvature in a slope
  ## weight grows like s^2, and Adam's step is measured in the weight, which shrinks like 1 / s
  for (s in c("A", "B")) local({
    s <- s
    observeEvent(list(input[[paste0("alg", s)]], input$xscale), {
      a <- input[[paste0("alg", s)]]
      base <- c(gdfix = 0.1, sgdls = 0.1, mom = 0.03, adam = 0.1)[a]
      if (!is.null(a) && !is.na(base)) {
        v <- unname(base) / xsc()^(if (a == "adam") 1 else 2)
        r <- LRGRID[which.min(abs(log(LRGRID) - log(v)))]
        updateSelectInput(session, paste0("lr", s), selected = as.character(r))
      }
    })
  })
  observeEvent(input$setzero, theta0(rep(0, NP)))
  observeEvent(input$newstart, {
    rseed(rseed() + 1)
    th <- rand_start(rseed()); th[1:J] <- th[1:J] / xsc()   # random weights for x / s
    theta0(th)
  })
  ## an arrow click moves the nearest arrow's weight by one step
  observeEvent(input$netv_click, {
    cl <- input$netv_click
    d <- ((cl$x - ARROWS$ax) / 0.05)^2 + ((cl$y - ARROWS$ay) / 0.04)^2
    i <- which.min(d)
    if (d[i] < 2) {
      th <- theta0()
      th[ARROWS$idx[i]] <- th[ARROWS$idx[i]] + ARROWS$dir[i] * as.numeric(input$astep)
      theta0(th)
    }
  })

  ## the predictor on a different scale: x -> s x, with the slope weights of the generating
  ## network divided by s, so the true curve is the same function of x / s
  xsc <- reactive(if (is.null(input$xscale)) 1 else as.numeric(input$xscale))
  TT <- reactive({ th <- TRUE_THETA; th[1:J] <- th[1:J] / xsc(); th })
  observeEvent(input$settrue, theta0(TT()))
  ## a new scale of x keeps the starting curve: the slope weights change with it
  xprev <- reactiveVal(1)
  observeEvent(input$xscale, {
    th <- theta0(); th[1:J] <- th[1:J] * xprev() / xsc(); xprev(xsc()); theta0(th)
  }, ignoreInit = TRUE)
  DAT <- reactive({
    D <- make_data(input$n, dseed())
    D$x <- D$x * xsc()
    D
  })
  ## one run for each optimizer, from the same start on the same data
  mkrun <- function(s) reactive({
    D <- DAT(); a <- input[[paste0("alg", s)]]
    if (is.null(a) || a == "none") return(NULL)
    fixed <- a %in% c("gdfix", "sgdls", "mom", "adam")
    req(!fixed || !is.null(input[[paste0("lr", s)]]))
    run_alg(a, theta0(), D$x, D$y, as.numeric(input$maxit),
            tol = if (is.null(input$gtol)) 1e-6 else as.numeric(input$gtol),
            patience = if (is.null(input$stall)) Inf else as.numeric(input$stall),
            lr  = if (fixed) as.numeric(input[[paste0("lr", s)]]) else NA,
            mom = if (a == "mom") input[[paste0("mom", s)]] else NA,
            m   = if (a %in% MINIBATCH) as.numeric(input[[paste0("batch", s)]]) else NA)
  })
  runA <- mkrun("A"); runB <- mkrun("B")
  ## the network panels show the run chosen in "Network of"
  netsel <- reactive(if (identical(input$netsel, "B") && !is.null(runB())) "B" else "A")
  run <- reactive(if (netsel() == "B") runB() else runA())

  ## the browser owns the iteration (slider, play timer, buttons); a new run restarts it
  observeEvent(list(runA(), runB()), {
    nmax <- max(runA()$n, if (is.null(runB())) 0L else runB()$n)
    session$sendCustomMessage("krun", list(max = nmax - 1L,
                                           play = isTRUE(input$autoplay) && nmax > 1))
  })
  kraw <- reactive(as.integer(if (is.null(input$kshow)) 0L else input$kshow))
  kpos <- reactive(min(kraw(), run()$n - 1L))

  cur <- reactive({
    R <- run(); k <- min(kpos(), R$n - 1L) + 1L
    list(R = R, k = k, th = R$P[k, ], g = R$G[k, ])
  })

  output$netv <- renderPlot({
    C <- cur(); R <- C$R
    vmax <- max(3, quantile(abs(R$P), 0.95))
    par(mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1))
    draw_net(C$th, vmax, as.numeric(input$ctr),
             sprintf("%s: weights, iteration %d   (loss %.4f)", netsel(), C$k - 1L, R$F[C$k]))
  })

  output$netg <- renderPlot({
    C <- cur()
    gmax <- max(1e-8, max(abs(C$g)))
    par(mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1))
    draw_net(C$g, gmax, as.numeric(input$ctr),
             sprintf("%s: gradient of the loss, iteration %d", netsel(), C$k - 1L),
             arrows = FALSE, digits = 3)
  })

  ## one clearly different colour per hidden unit
  PCOL <- c("#F28E00", "#1F5FBF", "black", "#00B5CC")

  output$fit <- renderPlot({
    RA <- runA(); RB <- runB(); R <- RA; D <- DAT(); kk <- kraw()
    xg <- seq(-3, 3, length.out = 300) * xsc()
    par(mar = c(4, 4.2, 2.5, 1))
    plot(D$x, D$yj, pch = 19, cex = 0.7,
         col = adjustcolor("#E8820C", 0.5), ylim = c(0, max(D$y) + 1),
         xlab = "x", ylab = expression(lambda(x) ~ "and counts y"),
         main = "fitted mean and the generated data")
    lines(xg, lambda_fun(TT(), xg), col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)
    lines(xg, lambda_fun(R$P[1, ], xg), col = "grey60", lwd = 2)
    lines(xg, lambda_fun(RA$P[min(kk, RA$n - 1L) + 1L, ], xg), col = "#2E8B57", lwd = 3)
    if (!is.null(RB))
      lines(xg, lambda_fun(RB$P[min(kk, RB$n - 1L) + 1L, ], xg), col = "#1F5FBF", lwd = 2.5)
    leg <- data.frame(
      lab = c("true mean", "starting weights", paste("A:", alg_name(input$algA)), "counts"),
      lwd = c(2, 2, 3, NA), lty = c(2, 1, 1, NA), pch = c(NA, NA, NA, 19),
      col = c("red", "grey60", "#2E8B57", adjustcolor("#E8820C", 0.7)),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    if (!is.null(RB))
      leg <- rbind(leg, data.frame(lab = paste("B:", alg_name(input$algB)), lwd = 2.5, lty = 1,
                                   pch = NA, col = "#1F5FBF", stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
    legend("topright", bty = "n", cex = 0.78, lwd = leg$lwd, lty = leg$lty,
           pch = leg$pch, col = leg$col, legend = leg$lab)
  })

  ## the same fit on the log scale, where the units simply add up
  output$eta <- renderPlot({
    C <- cur(); xg <- seq(-3, 3, length.out = 300) * xsc()
    VH <- unit_terms(C$th, xg)
    eta <- C$th[3 * J + 1] + rowSums(VH)
    eta_true <- log(lambda_fun(TT(), xg))
    par(mar = c(4, 4.2, 2.5, 1))
    matplot(xg, VH, type = "l", lty = 3, lwd = 2.5, col = PCOL,
            ylim = pmax(-8, pmin(8, range(VH, eta, eta_true))),
            xlab = "x", ylab = expression(log ~ lambda(x)),
            main = "log scale: the scaled units v_j h_j add up to the fit")
    abline(h = 0, lty = 3, col = "grey70")
    lines(xg, eta_true, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)
    lines(xg, eta, col = "#2E8B57", lwd = 3)
    legend("topright", bty = "n", cex = 0.78, ncol = 2,
           lwd = c(rep(2.5, J), 3, 2), lty = c(rep(3, J), 1, 2),
           col = c(PCOL, "#2E8B57", "red"),
           legend = c(paste0("v", 1:J, " h", 1:J), "sum + v0 (fit)", "true"))
  })

  output$conv <- renderPlot({
    R <- runA(); RF <- runB(); C <- list(R = R, k = min(kraw(), R$n - 1L) + 1L)
    it <- 0:(R$n - 1)
    gn <- sqrt(rowSums(R$G^2))
    par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4.2, 2.5, 1))
    xl <- c(0, max(R$n, if (is.null(RF)) 0 else RF$n) - 1)
    ## the loss on the scale chosen below: as is, its log10, or the log10 of its excess
    ## over the smallest value either run reaches (so differences near the floor show)
    sc <- if (is.null(input$lscale)) "log" else input$lscale
    best <- min(c(R$F, RF$F), na.rm = TRUE)
    ls_fun <- function(v) switch(sc, lin = v, log = log10(pmax(v, 1e-12)),
                                 exc = log10(pmax(v - best, 1e-12)))
    ls_lab <- switch(sc, lin = "loss", log = expression(log[10] ~ "loss"),
                     exc = expression(log[10] ~ "(loss - smallest reached)"))
    plot(it, ls_fun(R$F), type = "b", pch = 20, col = "#2E8B57", xlab = "iteration",
         ylab = ls_lab, xlim = xl, ylim = range(c(ls_fun(R$F), ls_fun(RF$F)), finite = TRUE),
         main = "average negative log-likelihood")
    if (!is.null(RF)) {
      lines(0:(RF$n - 1), ls_fun(RF$F), type = "b", pch = 20, col = "#1F5FBF")
      kb <- min(kraw(), RF$n - 1L)
      points(kb, ls_fun(RF$F[kb + 1L]), pch = 19, col = "#1F5FBF", cex = 1.6)
      legend("topright", bty = "n", cex = 0.8, lty = 1, pch = 20,
             col = c("#2E8B57", "#1F5FBF"),
             legend = c(paste("A:", alg_name(input$algA)), paste("B:", alg_name(input$algB))))
    }
    points(it[C$k], ls_fun(R$F[C$k]), pch = 19, col = "#2E8B57", cex = 1.6)
    gnr <- if (is.null(RF)) NULL else log10(sqrt(rowSums(RF$G^2)))
    plot(it, log10(gn), type = "b", pch = 20, col = "#2E8B57", xlab = "iteration",
         xlim = xl, ylim = range(c(log10(gn), gnr), finite = TRUE),
         ylab = expression(log[10] ~ "||gradient||"), main = "gradient norm")
    if (!is.null(RF)) {
      lines(0:(RF$n - 1), gnr, type = "b", pch = 20, col = "#1F5FBF")
      points(kb, gnr[kb + 1L], pch = 19, col = "#1F5FBF", cex = 1.6)
    }
    points(it[C$k], log10(gn[C$k]), pch = 19, col = "#2E8B57", cex = 1.6)
  })

  output$info <- renderUI({
    D <- DAT(); kk <- kraw()
    line <- function(R, a, tag, col) {
      k <- min(kk, R$n - 1L) + 1L; al <- R$A[k]
      paste0("<b style='color:", col, "'>", tag, ": ", alg_name(a), "</b> &nbsp; <b>",
             if (a %in% MINIBATCH) "epoch" else "iteration", "</b> ", k - 1L, " of ", R$n - 1L,
             " &nbsp; <b>loss</b> ", formatC(R$F[k], digits = 5, format = "f"),
             " &nbsp; <b>||gradient||</b> ", formatC(sqrt(sum(R$G[k, ]^2)), digits = 3, format = "g"),
             if (is.finite(al)) paste0(" &nbsp; <b>",
                                       if (a %in% c("gdfix", "mom", "adam")) "learning rate"
                                       else "step length", "</b> ",
                                       formatC(al, digits = 3, format = "g")) else "",
             "<br><i>", R$note, "</i>")
    }
    HTML(paste(line(runA(), input$algA, "A", "#2E8B57"),
               if (!is.null(runB())) line(runB(), input$algB, "B", "#1F5FBF"),
               sep = "<br>"))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
````

::::

This app accompanies *[Optimization for Maximum Likelihood Estimation](../compstat_book/chapters/unit05_MLE.html#backprogation-algorithm-for-neural-networks)* in the book.
